ceiling_statement: Resource-normalized throughput of any H1–H8 system on p workers is bounded by T_p ≥ max(W/p, S, n·c_commit): W = total verification/generation work, S = span (critical path) of the input dependency DAG, and n·c_commit = the irreducibly SERIAL cost of appending n accountable transitions to the single-writer monotonic certificate sequence (H4/H6). Verification work W itself has an information-theoretic floor: a zero-producer-trust verifier (H8, recompute-and-compare) must read and hash every committed byte at least once, so throughput can never exceed the declared hardware's min(I/O bandwidth, hash bandwidth) per admitted byte; on unchanged inputs, content-addressed memoization reduces work to the delta plus one digest comparison per cached unit — its floor. The ceiling is attained by a deterministic parallel-map with ordered serial fold: embarrassingly parallel per-item verification saturating p workers, a single serialized commit seat with O(log n) Merkle proof material per append, and all bounds (worker count, batch sizes, item ranges) derived from committed corpus configuration rather than constants.
derivation: (1) Serial-commit floor: H4 (single-writer canonical truth) plus H6 (monotonic, all-or-nothing certificate sequence) force a total order on admissions — a single-copy linearizable log; by the standard consistency argument a totally ordered certificate chain cannot be committed by two writers concurrently without either forking the sequence (violating H6 monotonicity) or coordinating through what is again a single serialization point; hence commit throughput is bounded by the sequential rate of that point, and the best achievable is to make c_commit small (constant hashing per append, O(log n) proof size — the known optimum for verifiable append-only structures). (2) Work/span law (Brent): any schedule of the dependency DAG on p workers has makespan ≥ max(W/p, S) — a scheduling limit independent of implementation. (3) Verification floor: under H8 the verifier may not trust any declared root, so trusting k bytes requires reading k bytes — Ω(k) I/O and Ω(k) hashing; sublinear verification requires succinct proof systems (SNARKs) whose trusted setup and toolchain fall outside 'feasible today with standard cryptography', so recompute-and-compare's linear cost is the operative floor and hash/I-O bandwidth of the declared resources the operative ceiling. (4) Determinism costs nothing asymptotically: H5 forbids nondeterministic result order, but parallel-map with a deterministic ordered reduction (fixed item indexing, merge by index) achieves the same T_p bound while producing byte-identical output to sequential execution — the H5 tax on throughput is zero, so any design paying throughput for determinism is below ceiling.
attainment_mechanism: All components have B0 seats: the parallel work tier is lparallel one-file-per-article in systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/frbr-pipeline-stage.lisp and systems/orchestrator-core/parallel-executor.lisp; the serial commit seat is the single writer (systems/orchestrator-omega-modules/unified-frbr-generator.lisp / emit-graph in source/write-authority.lisp) feeding the RFC-6962 Merkle append in source/merkle-authority.lisp (O(log n) inclusion/consistency proofs, already CVE-2012-2459-safe); the delta floor is systems/orchestrator-core/artifact-cache.lisp content-addressed memoization; the 3000-event chain in systems/orchestrator-cli/inference-gate.lisp shows the verification tier already runs at scale. To reach ceiling today: (a) replace the parallel executor's error-swallowing with fail-closed per-tier all-or-nothing completion (condition propagates, tier aborts — H3/H6), (b) impose deterministic ordered reduction (merge worker results by article index before commit — H5), (c) derive the article bound from corpus configuration (the seat already exists as *constitution-articles* in structure.lisp) instead of a literal type bound, (d) persist throughput numbers into the same hash-chained cost ledger as AX-17 so scale claims are replayable artifacts, not prose.

lean_obligation: Theorem (schedule optimality with serial accountable commit): for a dependency DAG G with work W and span S, and a commit relation forced total-ordered by H4/H6 with per-item cost c, every conforming schedule on p workers satisfies `T_p ≥ max (W / p) (max S (n * c))`, and the ordered-parallel-map/serial-fold schedule satisfies `T_p ≤ W / p + S + n * c` while producing output extensionally equal to the sequential schedule (`parExec G = seqExec G`, determinism under H5). Verification floor lemma: any sound verifier `V` with zero producer trust over committed byte string `b` satisfies `reads V ≥ |b|` (if V never reads index i, there exist two committed strings differing only at i that V cannot distinguish, contradicting soundness). Incremental floor: for cached unit u with unchanged digest, re-verification cost is exactly one digest comparison.
